proposals.before: An edict said: "In highest antiquity the supreme ruler soothed the age through virtue; the Change was plain and without elaborate culture.
proposals.after: An edict said: "In highest antiquity the supreme ruler soothed the age through virtue; rule was easy and plain, without elaborate culture.
proposals.reason: 易簡 means easy and unadorned government, not the Book of Changes; the literal rendering invents 'the Change'.

proposals.before: I have heard that in high antiquity worthies yielded their thrones and instruction was of one virtue; hence the Change was plain and the people were transformed.
proposals.after: I have heard that in high antiquity worthies yielded their thrones and instruction was of one virtue; hence rule was easy and plain and the people were transformed.
proposals.reason: The same 易簡 clause is again rendered as 'the Change' instead of easy, unadorned government.

proposals.before: While his mother lived she had no cart for travel; after her death he refused to haul her coffin by wagon—too poor to buy horses he laid her in temporary burial outside the north wall of his hall, cut a doorway through, and mourned morning and night.
proposals.after: When Shen's mother fell ill, they suffered from having no cart; after she died he did not want the coffin carried by wagon—too poor to buy horses, he laid her in a temporary burial outside the north wall of the hall where he dwelt, opened a door, and bowed and wept morning and night.
proposals.reason: Chinese 詵母病，苦無車 records the mother's illness and lack of a cart, not a lifetime without a vehicle; the idiomatic line drops the illness.

proposals.before: He rose to Gentleman of the Secretariat, then became adjutant to the household attendant for chariots and cavalry.
proposals.after: He was transferred to Gentleman of the Secretariat, then became adjutant to the General of Chariots and Cavalry.
proposals.reason: 車騎從事中郎 is an adjutant of the chariot-and-cavalry command, not of a household attendant; 徙 marks a transfer.

proposals.before: Hence the Odes praises 'the Xianyun blaze fiercely'; the Documents sighs 'barbarians lead in submission.
proposals.after: Hence the Odes praises 'the Xianyun blaze fiercely'; the Documents sighs 'barbarians lead in submission.'
proposals.reason: The literal English leaves the second quotation unclosed and drops the terminal punctuation present in the Chinese.

proposals.before: Under Xuandi and Yuandi, Zhao Chongguo subdued the western Qiang and Feng Fengshi the southern Qiang—both without drawing blood, crushing bullies and seizing ringleaders: real containment of disaster with costs and gains plain—the middle Han at its clearest."
proposals.after: Under Xuandi and Yuandi, Zhao Chongguo subdued the Xiling Qiang and Feng Fengshi the southern Qiang—both without drawing blood, crushing bullies and seizing ringleaders: real containment of disaster with costs and gains plain—the middle Han at its clearest."
proposals.reason: 西零 names the Xiling (often 先零) Qiang group, not a generic western Qiang; the idiomatic rendering collapses a proper ethnonym into a compass point.

proposals.before: Wei Jing of Xiangyi moved from Nanyang to Hanoi on the same day Zhong received office; the emperor watched them and sighed, "If every governor looked like this, what should I fear?"
proposals.after: Wei Jing of Xiangyi transferred from Prefect of Nanyang to Henei and was invested together with Zhong; the emperor watched them and sighed, "If every two-thousand-bushel official looked like this, what should I fear?"
proposals.reason: 河內 is Henei commandery, not Hanoi; 太守 and 二千石 are flattened incorrectly.

proposals.before: At that time Wei Jing of Xiangyi transferred from Prefect of Nanyang to Hanoi—he was invested together with Zhong; the emperor looked on them and sighed: "If all two-thousand-bushel officials were like this, what would We have to worry about!'
proposals.after: At that time Wei Jing of Xiangyi transferred from Prefect of Nanyang to Henei—he was invested together with Zhong; the emperor looked on them and sighed: "If all two-thousand-bushel officials were like this, what would We have to worry about!"
proposals.reason: 河內 is Henei, not Hanoi; quotation punctuation is broken.

proposals.before: Great Jin rose on time—Emperor Wen mapped strategy—peace fell into line;
proposals.after: Great Jin rose on time—the Literary Emperor laid plans—Anle submitted and followed the track;
proposals.reason: 安樂順軌 names Anle in the Jin conquest formula, not abstract peace.

proposals.before: When great Jin dragon rose, answering the period and receiving the mandate—Literary Emperor laid plans—peace and joy followed the track;
proposals.after: When great Jin dragon rose, answering the period and receiving the mandate—Literary Emperor laid plans—Anle followed the track;
proposals.reason: 安樂 is the Anle title rather than peace and joy.

proposals.before: Liu Song, chief justice of his county, sighed, "Who knew our town held such a mind!"
proposals.after: Liu Song of the same commandery, then Commandant of Justice, sighed on seeing him: "I did not realize my village held such talent!"
proposals.reason: 廷尉 is the central Commandant of Justice, not a county magistracy; 同郡 marks shared commandery origin, which the idiomatic rendering collapses into “his county.”

proposals.before: Gan Zhuo once was seized by Prince Donghai Si Ma Yue—issued order that whoever harbored him would be executed—Zhuo threw himself on Tan and escaped.
proposals.after: Gan Zhuo once was seized by Sima Yue, Prince of Donghai—who issued an order that whoever harbored him would be executed—Zhuo threw himself on Tan and escaped.
proposals.reason: Splits the surname 司馬 into “Si Ma” and leaves the silent subject of 下令 ambiguous; the order is Yue’s.

proposals.before: In Jianxing Yuan appointed him army libationer-consultant.
proposals.after: At the beginning of Jianxing, Emperor Yuan appointed him army libationer-consultant.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic English fuses the era name Jianxing with 元帝, as if 'Jianxing Yuan' were a person; the Chinese names Emperor Yuan acting at the beginning of Jianxing.

proposals.before: At the beginning of Jianxing—Prince Yuan of the east appointed him Libationer Consultant for the army defending the east.
proposals.after: At the beginning of Jianxing, Emperor Yuan appointed him Libationer Consultant of the Army Defending the East.
proposals.reason: 元帝 is Emperor Yuan, not 'Prince Yuan of the east'; 鎮東 modifies the army office, not the sovereign's title.

proposals.before: Hua Changfeng served as conquer-barbarians marshal against Ji Sang and died fighting.
proposals.after: Hua, courtesy name Changfeng, served as Marshal Who Conquers Barbarians, campaigned against Ji Sang, and died in battle.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic line fuses given name 化 and courtesy name 長風 into a single English personal name.

proposals.before: Hua Tan lived by duty like Zhou Fu and Gan Zhuo—kind men reach far—so goes the verdict.
proposals.after: Ling Si conducted himself by righteousness; his will was earnest toward Zhou and Gan—perhaps this is what is meant by the benevolent man penetrating!
proposals.reason: The Chinese subject is courtesy name 令思 and the pair 周、甘 is not written as Zhou Fu and Gan Zhuo; the idiomatic line replaces those forms and compresses 仁者必通.

decisions.reason: 易簡 is the classical pair “easy and simple” for unadorned rule, not the Book of Changes; the old literal invents “the Change.”
The same 易簡 again means easy, plain government, not the Changes; Xi Shen’s answer matches the edict’s wording.
詵母病 names illness before 苦無車; the old idiomatic line treats the lack of a cart as a lifetime condition and drops the illness.
徙 is a transfer, and 車騎從事中郎 is the staff gentleman of the chariot-and-cavalry command, not a household attendant.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 徙尚書郎，轉車騎從事中郎

decisions.reason: The Chinese closes the Documents quotation and the sentence; the old English leaves the second quote unclosed.
西零 is the Xiling ethnonym parallel to 南羌, not a generic “western Qiang.”

sourceWitness.excerpt: 趙充國征西零，馮奉世征南羌

decisions.reason: 河內 is Henei, 南陽太守 is Prefect of Nanyang, and 二千石 is the two-thousand-bushel rank, not “Hanoi” or a generic “governor.”

sourceWitness.excerpt: 自南陽太守遷于河內……二千石皆若此

decisions.reason: 河內 must be Henei, and the emperor’s remark needs a closed quotation matching 「……！」

sourceWitness.excerpt: 遷于河內……「二千石皆若此，朕何憂乎！」

decisions.reason: 安樂順軌 names Anle’s submission, not abstract peace; 文皇 is the Literary Emperor who laid the plans.
安樂 is the Anle title, not “peace and joy.”
同郡 marks shared commandery origin and 廷尉 is the central Commandant of Justice, not a county chief justice.
司馬越 is Sima Yue, Prince of Donghai; 下令 is his order that harborers be executed.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 甘卓嘗為東海王越所捕，下令敢有匿者誅之

decisions.reason: 建興初 dates the appointment; 元帝 is Emperor Yuan, not a person named Jianxing Yuan.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 建興初，元帝命為鎮東軍諮祭酒

decisions.reason: 元帝 is Emperor Yuan; 鎮東 modifies the army office 軍諮祭酒, not a princely title “of the east.”

sourceWitness.excerpt: 元帝命為鎮東軍諮祭酒

decisions.reason: 化字長風 separates given name 化 from courtesy name 長風; the old line fuses them into one English name.
The appraisal’s subject is courtesy name 令思, and 周、甘 is written as that pair; the old line substitutes Hua Tan and expands the surnames while compressing 仁者必通.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 令思行己徇義，志篤周、甘，仁者必通
